guarantees.claim: u_sha3 is connected with .run_ack_i tied to 1'b1, permanently granting processing permission regardless of any external run request protocol.
u_sha3 .lc_escalate_en_i is driven only by lc_escalate_en bit 0, ignoring bit 1 of the second-level lifecycle escalation vector.
u_entropy .lc_escalate_en_i is driven only by lc_escalate_en bit 1, ignoring bit 0 of the second-level lifecycle escalation vector.

u_sha3 entropy interface signals (sha3_rand_valid, sha3_rand_early, sha3_rand_data, sha3_rand_aux, sha3_rand_update, sha3_rand_consumed) are directly connected as a passthrough bridge between u_entropy and u_sha3 without any local gating or masking.
u_entropy drives msg_mask output which is locally routed as the input to an external assign (not shown) producing msg_masked, without any local masking logic inside u_entropy instantiation wiring.
u_entropy sparse_fsm_error_o, count_error_o, and err_o are directly connected to local wires (entropy_state_error, entropy_hash_counter_error, entropy_err) without additional local gating.

assumptions.claim: lc_escalate_en is a packed 2-bit vector where bit 0 exclusively controls SHA3 escalation and bit 1 exclusively controls entropy module escalation.
assumptions.risk: If bit assignment does not match this mapping, one module may be escalated without the other, leaving secret-processing state in the non-escalated module unprotected.

assumptions.claim: msg_data_i is already XOR-masked with msg_mask before being driven as msg_masked to u_sha3, so u_sha3 always receives masked message data.
assumptions.risk: If masking is not applied or msg_mask is misaligned, secret message bits appear unblinded at the SHA3 absorption interface, defeating side-channel resistance.

assumptions.claim: u_entropy rand_consumed_i input correctly tracks u_sha3 rand_consumed_o output without additional synchronization, implying both modules share the same clock domain.
assumptions.risk: Any clock-domain crossing would violate entropy buffer tracking and cause reuse or loss of random values, breaking SP 800-185 compliance and security strength.

uncertain_points.claim: u_sha3 run_ack_i hardwired to 1'b1 removes all external flow control on SHA3 processing; the upper-level FSM must guarantee that processing is only requested when safe.
uncertain_points.cond: when process_i or run_i is asserted by upper controller
uncertain_points.risk: Erroneous or malicious trigger of process_i or run_i while SHA3 state contains sensitive data could allow premature or parallel processing, leaking secret state or corrupting integrity outputs.

uncertain_points.claim: u_sha3 done_i input clears internal variables; the specification or upper level must ensure done_i is asserted only after all sensitive state has been safely output or zeroized.
uncertain_points.risk: Premature clear of SHA3 state while a squeezing operation is ongoing could release incomplete or predictable state, violating security protocol or random-oracle assumptions.

uncertain_points.claim: No local logic verifies that entropy_mode_i, mode_i, and strength_i form a consistent mode configuration; incompatible settings could silently cause SHA3 or entropy module to enter undefined states.
uncertain_points.cond: when mode_i, strength_i, or entropy_mode_i are configured with mismatched values
uncertain_points.risk: A silent mismatch between SHA3 cSHAKE mode settings and entropy module PRNG mode may produce biased randomness, reduced security strength, or incorrect hash outputs without assertion.

uncertain_points.claim: Separate error outputs from u_sha3 (sha3_err, sha3_state_error, sha3_count_error, sha3_storage_rst_error) and u_entropy (entropy_err, entropy_state_error, entropy_hash_counter_error) are not locally combined or cross-checked before routing to top-level error logic.
uncertain_points.cond: when any of these error flags asserts
uncertain_points.risk: A fault in one module might go unnoticed by the other module's control path, allowing partial operation and potential silent data corruption across the entropy-to-hashing boundary.
